Arguments heard on : 29.01.2016 Judgment announced on : 29.01.2016 Brief facts of the case 1.In brief, the case of the prosecution is that on 20.02.2003 at about 06.00 p.m., Food Inspector Ranjeet Singh, Food Inspector Sh. S. B. Sharma and two Field Assistants under the supervision and directions of LHA Sh. S.C. Tyagi, visited the premises of M/s Aster Enterprises, X/925, Chand Mohalla, Gandhi Nagar, Delhi 110031,where accused Hari Shankar Sharma who was the vendor cum Proprietor was found present conducting the business of sale of various food articles including Packaged Drinking Water, for sale for human consumption and in compliance of the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as the PFA Act & PFA Rules) the Food Inspector collected/ purchased the sample of Packaged Drinking Water.
2.During the course of investigation, it was revealed that Sant Kumar Chopra S/o Sh. Manohar Lal,
was the VendorCumproprietor of M/s Aster Enterprises, X/925, Chand Mohalla, Gandhi Nagar,
Delhi 110031 at the time of sampling and as such he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop.

3.The investigation also revealed that the vendor/ accused Sant Kumar Chopra has purchased the sampled commodity from M/s. Sai Durga Aqua Mineral (P) Ltd. G6, Udyog Kunj, Industrial Area,
Ghaziabad 201302.

4.It is further the prosecution's case that the sample was sent to Public Analyst for analysis and as per the report of Public Analyst the sample was not conforming to standard because aerobic microbial count exceeded the prescribed maximum limit of 100 colonies per ml at 20 to 22 degree Celcius in 72 hours on agar and agar and the sample was also misbranded as there is violation of Rule 32 (e) and (f) of PFA Rules 1955.

Accordingly after obtaining the necessary Sanction / Consent under Section 20 of the Act, the present complaint was filed for violation of provisions of Section 2 (ia) (b) (h) & (l) of the PFA Act 1954 and also violated the Rule 32 (e) & (f) of PFA Rules, 1955 which is punishable under Section 16 of the Act read with Section 7 of the PFA Act.

5.After the complaint was filed, the accused was summoned vide orders dated 27.08.2003.
6.Notice for the violation of Section 2 (ia) (b) (h) & (l) of PFA Act 1954 punishable u/s 16 (1) (A) read with Section 7 of the PFA Act, 1954 was framed against the accused Sant Kumar Chopra vide order dated 18.01.2010 to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
7.The accused no. 02 M/s Sai Durga Aqua Minerals (Pvt) Ltd. was proceeded ex parte vide order dated 14.07.2009.
The accused no. 03 and 04 (Directors of accused no. 2) were declared as Proclaimed Offender vide order dated 24.11.2001 respectively.
8.Statement of accused no. 01 Sant Kumar Chopra was recorded U/s 313 Cr. P.C on 19.12.2014 wherein the accused Sant Kumar Chopra claimed himself to be innocent.
Despite opportunity given to accused, he did not lead any defence.

A brief scrutiny of the evidence recorded in the matter is as under:
9.PW1 Sh. S.C. Tyagi, has deposed that on 20.02.2003, he was posted as SDM/LHA, Gandhi Nagar, Delhi.

He deposed that on that day he alongwith Food Inspector Ranjeet Singh and FI. Sh.
S.B. Sharma and two FAs visited the premises of M/s. Aster Enterprises at X/925, Chand Mohalla,
Gandhi Nagar, Delhi, where accused Sant Kumar Chopra was found and conducting the business of packaged drinking water for sale for human consumption, which was lying in sealed polythene pouches of 300 ml each bearing identical label declaration.
He deposed that thereafter, they disclosed their identity and intention to purchase a sample of packaged drinking water from the accused for which he agreed.

He deposed that before starting sample proceedings, FI requested some passersby and neighbours to join in sample proceedings but none agreed and then, on request of FI Ranjeet Singh, FI S.B. Sharma agreed and joined as a witness in sample proceedings.

He deposed that thereafter, at about 6 pm, FI Ranjeet Singh purchased 30 sealed polythene pouches of packaged drinking water bearing identical label declaration from the accused on payment of Rs. 60/ vide vendor's receipt Ex.PW1/A bearing signature of vendor at point A.

He deposed that the so purchased sample of packaged drinking water was divided into three equal parts then and there by FI by putting these into three clean and dry jars i.e. 10 sealed polythene pouches of packaged drinking water were put in each of the jar.
He deposed that all the three jars containing Da vs .

3
the sample of packaged drinking water were packed, fastened marked and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules.

He deposed that LHA slips bearing his signature and code number were affixed on all the three counterparts in such as manner so as to appear partly on LHA Slips and partly on wrapper of the counterpart.

He deposed that Notice in Form VI was prepared vide Ex. PW1/B bearing signature of vendor at point A and a copy of the same was given to the vendor as per his endorsement at portion X to X on Ex. PW1/B.
He deposed that Panchnama Ex.PW1/C bearing signature of vendor at point A was also prepared.

10.He deposed that vendor disclosed the source of purchase of the sample commodity on Notice in Form VI at portion Y to Y that he had purchased the same from M/s. Sai Durga Aqua Mineral Pvt.
Ltd., G6, Udhyog Kunj Industrial Area, Ghaziabad vide Bill No. 981 Dated 01.02.2003 and accordingly, Notice U/Sec. 14 A of PFA Act addressing to M/s.

PW1/E bearing his signature at point A and provided the photocopy of the Purchase Bill Mark A to the FI at the spot bearing his signature at point A.

He deposed that all these documents Ex.PW1/A to Ex.PW1/D were read over and explained by the FI to the vendor and witness in vernacular Hindi and after understanding the same vendor signed at point A, witness signed at point B and FI signed the same at point C.

He deposed that two counterparts of the sample alongwith two copies of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet in intact condition were deposited with him on next working day i.e.
21.02.2003 vide LHA Receipt Ex.PW1/F bearing his signature of FI at point B, under intimation that one counterpart of the same has been deposited with PA on the same date.
He deposed that the PA Report was received which is Ex. PW1/G and as per the opinion of the PA mentioned at portion X, the sample was found not conforming to the standards as well as misbranded.

He deposed that after receipt of PA Report, he directed the FI to conduct the investigation and after completion of the investigation the FI put the entire case file before me and he forwarded the same, the then Director PFA Sh. S.L. Bansal, who after going through the same accorded his consent for institution of the case which is Ex. PW1/H bearing signature of Sh. S.L. Bansal at point A.
He deposed that thereafter, the complaint Ex.PW1/1 was filed in the Court by Food Inspector Ranjeet Singh.

11.During his cross examination, he stated that he does not remember as to total how many pouches of 300 ml of packaged drinking water were lying in the shop of the accused at that time, besides the pouches which were lifted as sample.
He stated that the vendor disclosed the source of purchase of the sample commodity at the spot.
He further stated that the Purchase Bill Ex. PW1/DA is the original of photocopy of Purchase Bill Mark A.
He admitted that there was no leakage in the sample commodity and it was sealed in original condition as such.

He admitted that vendor disclosed that the sealed pouches of packaged drinking water were the same which he had purchased from M/s.
Sai Durga Aqua Pvt. Ltd.
He admitted that the brand name of the product was 'Barshaa'.
12.PW2 Sh. Ranjeet Singh also deposed on the same lines as PW1.
He further deposed that he sent a letter Ex. PW2/B and reminder Ex. PW2/B1 to Sai Durga Aqua Minerals(P) Ltd., but no reply from them was received.
He deposed that he sent a letter to Joint Director BIS vide Ex. PW2/C and a letter to CMO, Ghaziabad Vide Ex. PW2/C1, but did not received their reply.
He deposed that he also sent a letter to STO, Ward No. 79 vide Ex. PW2/D and received its reply at portion X that no such Da vs .

Sant Kumar Chopra Page 1/11 on 29 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121168862/
4
firm M/s Aster Enterprises was registered in that ward.

He deposed that he personally visited the Office of Deputy Commissioner Sales Tax Ghaziabad and received their reply vide Ex. PW2/E to the effect that Sai Durga Aqua Mineral (P) Ltd, was having two directors, namely, Sh. Pawan Kumar (Since P.O.) and Sh. Amarjeet Kumar (Since P.O.).

He deposed that after conclusion of investigations, he put the entire case file before SDM/LHA concerned who forwarded the same to Sh. S. L. Bansal, the then Director PFA for obtaining his consent and Sh. S. L. Bansal granted his consent for prosecution Ex. PW1/H bearing his signature at point A.
He deposed that he filed the complaint before this Hon'ble Court vide Ex. PW1/I, bearing his signature at point A.

He deposed that he has brought the office file containing copy of intimation letter and has also brought original dispatch register for sending the intimation letter and copy of PA report to accused persons.
He deposed that these intimations letters and copy of PAs report were sent to accused persons through registered post through SDM/LHA.

He deposed that the intimation letter sent to accused Sant Kumar Chopra was not received back undelivered but the intimation letter sent to other accused persons were received back undelivered and then he tried to serve personally the intimation letter to other accused persons at their business as well as residential premises but these premises were found locked and some bank seal was found affixed on these premises.
He deposed that the photocopy of office copy of intimation letter is Ex. PW2/A, bearing signature of LHA at point A and the photocopy of dispatch register is Ex. PW2/B.

He deposed that the returned intimation letters along with postal envelopes are collectively and respectively Ex. PW2/C, PW2/C1, PW2/C2 and Ex. PW2/C3.
13.During
his cross examination
, he stated that as per the practice of Department no AD card is sent with registered dak to the addressee when any letter was sent to them.

He voluntarily stated that he made personal efforts also to serve the intimation letter upon accused Sant Kumar Chopra and he met him in this regard and he told that he had received the intimation letter along with copy of PA's report.
He stated that however Sant Kumar Chopra did not give this fact in writing to him.
He stated that he does not remember the date of his visit to Sant Kumar Chopra in this regard.
He denied the suggestion that the intimation letter along with copy of PA report was not served on the accused either by post or personally.
He stated that more than 100 pouches of the sample commodity were lying in the gunny bag in the shop of the accused at that time.
He admitted that the pouches of the sample commodity were in sealed condition at the time when he took the sample of the same and there was no leakage or breakage therein.
He admitted that vendor disclosed the source of purchase of the sample commodity and produced photocopy of bill of purchase of the same which is Mark A.
He admitted that as per the label declaration, the sample commodity was of 'Barshaa' brand.

He admitted that on his investigation he was satisfied that the sample commodity was supplied by M/s Sai Durga Aqua Mineral (P) Ltd. i.e. accused no. 2 to accused no. 1.
14.This
so far is the evidence in the matter.
15. Ld. counsel for accused no. 1 has argued that accused no. 1 cannot be held liable for the adulteration as he was merely a vendor/retailer and not manufacturer of sample product.

He has also urged for giving benefit of warranty as envisaged u/s 19 (2) r/w section 14 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 to the accused, as he purchased the sample commodity from Sai Durga Acqua Minerals (P) Ltd in the same condition.
The Ld. SPP for the complainant has contended the Da vs .

Sant Kumar Chopra Page 1/11 on 29 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121168862/
5 contrary.
16.I
have heard the arguments advanced at bar by the Ld. defence counsel as also the Ld. SPP for complainant.
I have also carefully gone through the evidence recorded in the matter and perused the documents placed on record by the prosecution in this case.

Warranty 17.It shall be useful here to reproduce Section 14 and Section 19 (2) of PFA Act, which read as under : "Section 19 (2):A vendor shall not be deemed to have committed an offence pertaining to the sale of any adulterated or misbranded article of food if he proves  (a) that he purchased the article of food  (i) in a case where a licence is prescribed for the sale thereof, from a duly licensed manufacturer,
distributor or dealer,
(ii) in any other case, from any manufacturer, distributor or dealer, with a written warranty in the prescribed form; and (b) that the article of food while in his possession was properly stored ;and that he sold it in the same state as he purchased it."
18.Section 14 of the Act also provides as under: "Manufacturers, distributors and dealers to give warranty  No (manufacturer or distributor of, or dealer in) any article of food shall sell such article to any vendor unless he also gives a warranty in writing in the prescribed form about the nature and quality of such article to the vendor:
[Provided that a bill, cash memorandum or invoice in respect of the sale of any article of food given by a manufacturer or distributor of, or dealer in, such article to the vendor thereof shall be deemed to be a warranty given by such manufacturer,
distributor or dealer under this section.].
19.In order to seek benefit of section 19(2) r/w section 14 of the Act, vendor was obliged to prove (a)
he had purchased the article of food in question from the manufacturer/distributor or dealer with a written warranty in the prescribed form; (b) the article of food was purchased, was properly stored while it was in his possession and (c) he sold in the same state which was purchased by him.
20.Proviso of Section 14 creates a fiction that a bill, cash memo or invoice given by distributor or dealer to the vendor shall be deemed to be a warranty.

sentences.text: Hence, even if the vendor is unable to produce a warranty in Form VIA, the bill or cash memo given to him by the manufacturer or distributor will be enough to satisfy the requirements of sub section (2) of Section 19 of the Act.

6
21.In Pothuri Ananda Venkta Shubha Rao Gupta Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh 1991 FAC 79

entities.text: Pothuri Ananda Venkta Shubha Rao Gupta Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh 1991 FAC 79
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , it was held that the burden is on the accused to produce the warranty and prove that he purchased the food article under warranty from a particular person.
Mere filing of the photocopy of the bill / the warranty without filing the original in the court will not be of any help of the accused / the vendor.

22.In the case at hand, the accused no. 01 disclosed to the FI at the time of lifting of the sample that he purchased the sampled sealed polythene pouches of Packaged Drinking Water from Sai Durga Acqua Mineral (P) Ltd by Bill No. 981 dated 01.02.2003 as manifested from the endorsement at point Y to Y made by accused on Form VI Ex. PW1/B.

The same is also corroborated by the testimony of PW1 and PW2 who deposed that the accused no. 01 disclosed the source of purchase at M/s Sai Durga Aqua Mineral (P) Ltd at the time of preparation of Form VI at the spot.
The PW2 also stated in his deposition that the accused no. 01 also produced the photocopy of bill of purchase of sample commodity at the spot.

The primary witness PW2 FI Ranjeet Singh also stated during his testimony that during investigation it was found that sample commodity was processed/packed and supplied to the vendor/accused no. 01 by M/s Sai Durga Aqua Mineral (P) Ltd (accused no. 02).
The accused no. 01 also produced on record the original bill no. 981 dated 01.02.2003 Ex.PW1/DA.
The Ex.PW1/DA also bears the signature of authorized signatory of accused no. 2 M/s Sai Durga Aqua Minerals (Pvt) Ltd alongwith stamp of M/s. Sai Durga Aqua Minerals (Pvt) Ltd.

The genuineness of the bill of purchase Ex.PW1/DA is also established by the testimony of PW1 and PW2.
23.Both
the primary witness PW1 and PW2 also admitted during their cross examination that there was no leaking in the sample commodity and it was sealed in original condition as such.

So, its stand prove that the accused no. 01 purchased the sample commodity from accused no. 02 by way of written warranty in the form of a bill and the accused no. 01 properly stored the sample commodity and sold it in the same condition as it purchased from accused no. 02.

Thus, the accused no. 01 has fulfilled all the parameters for becoming entitled to benefit of warranty envisaged under 19(2) r/w Section 14 of PFA Act and cannot be held responsible for adulteration and misbranding of sample commodity.

So, the accused no. 1 (Sant Kumar Chopra) is acquitted for 16 (1)(A) read with Section 7 of the PFA Act, 1954 for violating Section 2 (ia) (b) (h) & (l) of PFA Act 1954 and Rule 32 (e) & (f) of PFA Rules, 1955.
23.It stands proved on record that the accused no. 2 (M/s. Sai Durga Aqua Minerals (Pvt) Ltd.)
supplied the sample commodity to accused no. 1 (Sant Kumar Chopra).

As far as, M/s. Sai Durga Aqua Minerals (Pvt) Ltd is concerned, it did not appear in the Court after service of process/
issuance of summons and was proceeded ex parte as is reflected in the proceedings dated 14.07.2009.
Its Directors 1) Pawan Kumar and 2) Amardeep Kumar, are already declared Proclaimed Offenders vide proceedings dated 24.11.2001.
On account of M/s.
Sai Durga Aqua Minerals (Pvt) Ltd having not challenged the prosecution story coupled with consistent and coherent testimony of PWs and the report of Public Analyst
, the accused M/s.
Sai Durga Aqua Minerals (Pvt) Ltd and its Directors are held liable for adulteration and misbranding as detected by Public Analyst.
Accordingly, accused no. 2 to 4 stand convicted of the charges in the present case.
It is ordered accordingly.
